oi.heading: Operating Income (Loss)
oi.text: The Company recognized an operating loss of $53,858,981 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to operating income of $1,862,325 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an unfavorable variance of $55,721,306. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company recognized an operating loss of $63,827,588, compared to operating income of $6,496,388 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, an unfavorable variance of $70,323,976. The change in operating results primarily reflects the $50,700,000 of non-cash stock-based compensation recognized in the third quarter of 2026 on the issuance of Series A Convertible Preferred Stock to the Chief Executive Officer, the non-cash equity-based compensation recognized in the first quarter of 2026, the $2,903,869 of bad debt expense recognized in the third quarter, higher media traffic purchase expense relative to revenue and lower revenue.

ga.heading: General & Administrative Costs
ga.text:
General and administrative expense was $55,772,470 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $529,562 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $55,242,908, or 10,431.8%. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, general and administrative expense was $67,069,720, compared to $1,238,398 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $65,831,322, or 5,315.8%. The prior-year amounts group professional fees with general and administrative expense to conform to the current-period caption.

The nine-month increase is predominantly non-cash. It includes $50,700,000 of stock-based compensation recognized in the third quarter on the issuance of Series A Convertible Preferred Stock to the Chief Executive Officer, $7,611,669 of stock-based compensation recognized on the January 1, 2026, vesting of the first tranche of his option award and $2,903,869 of bad debt expense recognized in the third quarter.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text: Interest expense was $1,232,771 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $38,009 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, interest expense was $2,909,860, compared to $51,277 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $2,848,723. Of the nine-month amount, $2,361,393 represents amortization of debt discount, original issue discount and deferred financing costs, including accelerated amortization recognized on notes converted during the period, consistent with the add-backs presented in the condensed consolidated statements of cash flows, and $548,467 represents stated and other interest, of which $354,562 relates to the Streeterville Notes and accretes to the outstanding balance rather than being paid in cash. Cash paid for interest was $77,842 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. See Note 9 — Debt Financing for further details.

net.heading: Net Loss
net.text: The Company recognized a net loss of $54,877,198, or $(1.38) per basic and diluted share, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to net income of $1,824,316, or $0.06 per basic and diluted share, for the three months ended September 30, 2025. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company recognized a net loss of $65,191,031, or $(1.73) per basic and diluted share, compared to net income of $6,445,111, or $0.21 per basic and diluted share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The change from net income to net loss is driven predominantly by non-cash charges rather than cash costs: $61,569,169 of stock-based compensation and shares issued for services, $2,903,869 of bad debt expense and $2,361,393 of debt discount, original issue discount and deferred financing cost amortization. Cash used in operating activities for the nine months was $8,540,512. The weighted-average number of common shares outstanding, basic and diluted, was 39,880,979 for the three months and 37,756,602 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 31,341,436 in each of the prior-year periods.

ocf.text: Net cash used in operating activities was $8,540,512 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $165,802, as revised, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Operating cash usage primarily reflects the increase in accounts receivable of $4,883,274 arising from the timing of customer collections and the settlement of previously accrued obligations, partially offset by non-cash add-backs in the reconciliation of net loss to operating cash flow, including stock-based compensation of $58,311,669, shares issued for services of $3,257,500 and amortization of debt discount, original issue discount and deferred financing costs of $2,361,393, less the $1,951,783 net gain on remeasurement of the compound embedded derivatives, $713,600 of marketable securities received as consideration and the $151,634 unrealized gain on marketable securities.

da.heading: Amortization and Depreciation
da.text: Amortization and depreciation expense was $735 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $48,643 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, a decrease of $47,908, or 98.5%. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, amortization and depreciation expense was $1,229, compared to $49,430 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, a decrease of $48,201, or 97.5%. The prior-year periods included $47,902 of amortization of original issue discount and deferred financing costs on notes payable, which for 2026 is presented within interest expense. The $1,476,856 of website and software development costs capitalized during 2026 had not been placed in service at September 30, 2026, and no amortization has been recognized.

sbc.text: For the three months ended September 30, 2026, general and administrative expense of $55,772,470 included $50,700,000 of stock-based compensation on the issuance of Series A Convertible Preferred Stock to the Chief Executive Officer, $2,903,869 of bad debt expense, $1,075,733 of net out-of-period reclassifications described in Note 2 ($1,145,733 reclassified from media traffic purchase expense — advertising and promotion of $814,598, filing fees of $220,025, insurance of $81,110 and legal fees of $30,000 — less $70,000 of consulting, advertising and office costs capitalized as software development costs) and $187,500 of other stock-based compensation. Excluding those items, third-quarter general and administrative expense was approximately $905,368, compared with approximately $1,829,816 of cash general and administrative expense in the second quarter.

wc.heading: Deferred Revenue
wc.text: No deferred revenue was outstanding at September 30, 2026, or December 31, 2025. The contract liability of $549,803 at March 31, 2026, was fully recognized as revenue during the three months ended June 30, 2026.

capex.heading: Property and Equipment, Net
capex.text: Furniture and equipment, net decreased by $1,229, from $14,919 at December 31, 2025, to $13,690 at September 30, 2026, reflecting depreciation for the period. In addition, the Company capitalized $1,476,856 of website and software development costs (none at December 31, 2025), of which $15,333 was included in payroll liabilities — related parties at September 30, 2026, and recorded a $180,000 investment in drone technology, of which $100,000 was included in accounts payable at September 30, 2026. See Note 5.

net sales.heading: Revenue
net sales.text: Total revenue was $3,729,807 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $4,913,318 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, a decrease of $1,183,511, or 24.1%. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, total revenue was $11,837,428, compared to $12,733,550 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, a decrease of $896,122, or 7.0%. Presented on the disaggregated basis in Note 4, digital advertising and media monetization revenue — comprising all revenue other than the Jet.AI and Braiin arrangements — was $3,729,807 and $10,023,828 for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared with $4,913,318 and $12,733,550 in the prior-year periods, while AI-driven marketing services revenue was nil and $1,813,600, with no comparable prior-year revenue. A portion of revenue was settled in non-cash consideration: equity securities with a fair value at receipt of $713,600 were received under customer contracts during the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

intro.text: Eva Live Inc. (the “Company”) was incorporated under the laws of the State of Nevada on August 27, 2002, as International Pit Boss Gaming, Inc. On October 1, 2002, the Company merged with Pro Roads Systems, Inc., a Florida corporation and a public shell company listed on the Pink Sheets. Pro Roads Systems, Inc. had no operations before the merger. The purpose of the merger was to change the Company’s domicile from Florida to Nevada. From its inception to 2006, the Company designed and developed software for the gaming industry. The Company changed its name on February 14, 2006, to Logo Industries Corporation and, on November 18, 2008, to Malwin Ventures Inc. On February 11, 2014, the Company announced negotiations with Impact Future Media LLC, and its President/Founder, Francois Garcia, acquired 100 % of Impact Future Media LLC and its media and entertainment assets.

StackAdapt is a self-serve DSP that relies on third-party data providers and contextual targeting.
In the future, we may rely on independent contractors to assist us in marketing and selling our products.
Our management relies on EBITDA, a non-GAAP financial metric that we believe help us to gauge the underlying performance of our business and to manage it effectively.

As we will only develop a limited number of products and services at a time, our overall success will depend on a limited number of products and services, which may cause variability and unsteady profits and losses depending on the products and services offered.
Our ability to raise the capital needed to improve our financial condition depends on the support from stockholders and its ability to obtain necessary equity financing.
Our survival depends on the success of our efforts to gain market acceptance and shares of our products and services in the U.S. debt management market, with the main focus on student loans.
We depend on our intellectual property, and our failure to protect that intellectual property could adversely affect our future growth and success.
Successfully expanding our business will depend on our ability to attract and manage staff, strategic business relationships, and shareholders.
Future success will depend on the Company’s ability to implement the technology correctly and on time.
The Company’s future success will depend on its ability to adapt to rapidly changing technologies by continually improving its products and services’ performance features and reliability.
We have relied upon cash from financing activities, and in the future, we intend to rely on revenues generated from operations to fund all the cash requirements of our activities.
As an “emerging growth company” under the JOBS act, we can rely on exemptions from certain disclosure requirements.
As a result, we are permitted to and intend to, rely on exemptions from certain disclosure requirements.
However, we cannot predict if investors will find our common stock less attractive because we may rely on these exemptions.

Declaration or payment of dividends, if any, will be at the discretion of our Board of Directors and will depend on our current financial condition, results of operations, capital requirements, and other factors deemed relevant by the Board of Directors.
The Company’s ability to continue as a going concern may depend on the success of management’s plans.
The ultimate realization of the deferred tax assets depends on generating future taxable income when those temporary differences become deductible.

The Company has entered into non-binding letters of intent with respect to the proposed acquisitions of Psquared Inc. and Airbeam Wireless Technologies Inc., formed Eva Defense Inc. to pursue acquisitions in the drone, autonomous systems and defense technology sectors, and invested $ 180,000 in drone technology during the third quarter (see Note 1 — Business Description and Nature of Operations).

On June 12, 2026, the Company announced that it had reached terms for a definitive agreement under which it would hold a 51 % ownership interest across Spiro Senior Living and related operating entities, subject to the completion of final documentation.
The Company’s $ 3,000,000 equity interest in Psquared Inc. is a non-marketable equity security without a readily determinable fair value.
In addition, the Company holds a $3,000,000 non-marketable equity interest in Psquared Inc. received in settlement of accounts receivable, which is classified as a non-current asset.
